name: Haredi Judaism
summary: Haredi Judaism is the strictly traditionalist wing of Orthodox Judaism, built around absolute authority of the Torah as the rabbis interpret it, full-time Torah study for men, and deliberate separation from secular culture. Its great rabbis are held to rule on all areas of life, politics included (da'at Torah), and most Haredim oppose a secular pre-messianic Jewish state while the movement also defends its institutions, schools and exemptions within the states where it lives.
scope: The mainstream Haredi world of the Hasidic courts and Lithuanian-style yeshiva communities as described by the Encyclopaedia Judaica and Haredi scholarship, with the councils of Agudath Israel (Moetzes Gedolei HaTorah, in America and in Israel) as its own voice. It excludes Modern Orthodoxy, religious Zionism and Satmar-style religious anti-Zionism (separate entries). Most economic, government, world and technology statements are null because the defining sources record no position; the movement's party and funding politics in Israel are the record of parties, not of the ideology.

change-traditions-that-no-longer-suit.rationale: The Encyclopaedia Judaica describes Haredim as holding tradition to be a sacred order of truths and customs that may not be abrogated, and as claiming to have made no compromises with the present.

clerical-rule.rationale: The doctrine of da'at Torah holds that the great religious authorities may rule in all areas of life, including the political realm, and Agudath Israel's policies are directed by its council of Torah sages.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Haredim see nothing inherently valuable in money apart from what it does to maintain the Jewish way of life, and there are frequent efforts to shun material pleasures.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Scholarship describes the Haredi worldview as putting conformity to group norms and collective solidarity above individual self-actualization and personal liberty.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Most Haredim see a pre-messianic state as religious hubris and the Moetzes forbids voting in Zionist elections, while a minority (some Sephardim, Chabad) is Zionist and Agudat Israel sits in the Knesset.

more-religion-public.rationale: Agudath Israel's 1974 proclamation urged Israel's leadership toward a 'wholehearted return to eternal Jewish values' as the answer to its problems.

premarital-sex.rationale: Haredim separate the sexes from early childhood, discourage dating, arrange marriages, and regulate sexual relations by Jewish law within marriage.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The Haredi view is that the only true merit is what the Torah and its accepted rabbinic interpretations prescribe, and that individuals are guided by those who know the law.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Haredim favour stringent over lenient readings of Jewish law, and their council rules that a movement rejecting the authority of the Torah and its Sages is outside Torah Judaism.

religion-illusion.rationale: Haredim treat their whole lives as service to God, and the Encyclopaedia Judaica presents religion as the purpose of existence, not a consolation that fades.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Haredim demand that the surrounding society protect their way of life or at least leave them alone.

religious-nation.rationale: The Moetzes holds that the Jewish people is defined by the Torah, and that the Zionist redefinition of it as a nation like all others is forbidden.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Agudath Israel's Torah council says the Torah forbids homosexual activity and sanctions only the union of a man and a woman, and rejects claims that same-sex marriage fits Jewish law.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Haredim use science, medicine and technology as instruments for serving God and keeping tradition, while holding that modernity has no value in itself.

traditional-family.rationale: Its statements call marriage between a man and a woman the 'bedrock relationship of the human family' and say discarding the historical definition is not a positive step for civilized society.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Haredim limit their contact with the outside world, yet Agudat Israel members stand for election and sit in the Knesset while refusing ministerial posts, and American Haredim vote as a bloc.

work-centre-of-life.rationale: Torah study for as long as possible is the ideal for men, and most adult men devote themselves to full-time study rather than gainful work.

notes: Themes searched: definition and scholarship (Encyclopaedia Judaica, da'at Torah scholarship, My Jewish Learning), Agudath Israel and Moetzes statements on marriage, Open Orthodoxy, Zionism, the Israeli draft, school choice, internet use and abortion. Positions of a single organisation on American policy (school vouchers) were left null because one organisation's policy is not shown to be part of the ideology; Israeli party politics and funding record is the parties', not the ideology's. Most economic, government, world and technology statements remain null: the defining sources are descriptive and state no position.
